etymologies.etymologyHTML: From earlier gamel, from Middle English *gamlen, *gamelen, variant of Middle English gamenen, from Old English gæmnian, gamnian, gamenian (“to joke; play”), related to Old English gamen (“joy; mirth; pleasure; entertainment; pastime; sport; game”), equivalent to game +‎ -le. Compare Old Danish gammel, Middle High German gamel (“pleasure; fun”). More at game.

definitions.definition: A significant risk, undertaken with a potential gain.
To take a risk, with the potential of a positive outcome.
To play risky games, especially casino games, for monetary gain.
To interact with equipment at a casino.
